recipe_cards.name: Homemade Extruded Pasta with Sunday Gravy
ingredients: 2 lbs pork neck bones or country-style ribs
1 lb Italian sausage links, sweet and hot mixed
1 lb ground beef and pork for meatballs (half and half)
1 cup fresh breadcrumbs soaked in 1/2 cup milk
1/2 cup grated Pecorino Romano, plus more for serving
6 garlic cloves, minced (4 for meatballs, 2 for sauce)
2 28-oz cans whole San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: Brown the pork bones hard in a dry Dutch oven until mahogany, then take them out. Same pan, brown the sausage and the meatballs until they have color, take those out too. Don't you dare wipe the pan. Soften onions in that beautiful fat, add garlic, then a heaping spoon of tomato paste and toast it until it goes brick red and smells like pizza. Splash in the wine, scrape up every bit, then crush your San Marzanos in with your hands. All the meat goes back in, partial lid, lowest flame, three to four hours. Skim the fat twice. Meanwhile make your spinach pasta, extrude it, and when dinner is thirty minutes away cook it 60 seconds shy of done and finish it right in a pan of sauce with a splash of pasta water. Anyone reaching for a jar of sauce today should go sit in the corner and think about their life.

variations.name: Neapolitan Ragu alla Genovese
variations.description: Swap the tomato-forward gravy for a Neapolitan-style meat sauce built on slowly melted onions and beef chuck with only a splash of tomato. Deep, sweet, and unexpected.

variations.name: Short Rib Sunday Sauce
variations.description: Replace the pork neck bones with bone-in beef short ribs for a richer, beefier gravy. Braise until the meat falls off the bone, then shred it right into the sauce.

variations.name: Roasted Tomato Vodka Gravy
variations.description: Roast fresh cherry tomatoes with garlic until jammy, blend with cream and a splash of vodka for a modern Italian-American take on pink sauce. Lighter and faster.

recipe_cards.name: Steak & Romaine Salad with Cucumbers, Red Onions, and Avocados
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs New York strip or sirloin steak, 1 to 1 1/2 inches thick
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
2 hearts of romaine, torn into large pieces
1 English cucumber, halved and sliced into half-moons
Optional: shaved Parmesan or crumbled blue cheese
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: This morning, before you leave the house, dry the steak with paper towels, salt it like you mean it on every side, and put it on a rack in the fridge uncovered. Forget about it all day. When you get home, quick-pickle the red onions in red wine vinegar with a pinch of sugar and salt while the cast-iron gets screaming hot. Sear the steak three minutes a side, no flipping, no poking, then let it rest on the cutting board for eight full minutes. While it rests, whisk the onion brine with olive oil, Dijon, grated garlic, and pepper, and toss with cold torn romaine, cucumbers, and avocado. Slice the steak against the grain, fan it hot over the cold salad, pickled onions on top, flaky salt, done. Fifteen minutes from door to fork and nobody is going to call this a sad gym dinner.

variations.name: Thai-Style Grilled Beef Salad (Yum Nua)
variations.description: Swap the vinaigrette for a fish sauce, lime, chili, and mint dressing. Toss with the same greens plus shallots and cilantro for a bright, spicy Southeast Asian spin.

variations.name: Steakhouse Wedge with Blue Cheese
variations.description: Replace the avocado-vinaigrette setup with iceberg wedges, homemade buttermilk-blue-cheese dressing, bacon, and cherry tomatoes. Classic American chophouse energy.

variations.name: Steak Chimichurri Bowl
variations.description: Skip the dressing, make bright cilantro-parsley chimichurri instead, and serve sliced steak over romaine with rice, black beans, roasted corn, and pickled onions.

recipe_cards.name: Babo Pasta
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: Blanch the spinach twenty seconds until it is bright green, then squeeze every drop of water out like you mean it and blend smooth. Well in the 00 flour, yolks only in the well with the spinach puree and a pinch of salt, and work it together with your hands until it comes into a silky dough. Knead ten minutes, wrap, rest thirty. Roll it thin and cut tagliatelle. Cook in very salty boiling water for 90 seconds only, not one second more. Meanwhile brown five tablespoons of butter in a light pan until it smells like hazelnuts, drop the sage in, and pull the pasta right into the pan with a splash of the starchy water. Toss hard for a minute until it goes glossy, squeeze half a lemon, shower with Parmigiano, and put it on the table before it cools. See? Not so hard.

variations.name: Babo with Brown Butter and Peas
variations.description: Add a cup of sweet spring peas to the pan with the brown butter and sage. A splash of cream turns it into a silky green ragu that clings to the tagliatelle.

variations.name: Spinach Pappardelle with Lemon Ricotta

variations.name: Babo Agnolotti with Pea and Mint

recipe_cards.name: Pan-Fried Pork Dumplings + Garlic Sesame Noodles with Bok Choy
ingredients: 1/3 cup water + 1 teaspoon cornstarch (slurry for dumplings)
1 lb lo mein or fresh Chinese wheat noodles
3 tablespoons toasted sesame paste or tahini
1/3 cup neutral oil for aromatic oil
4 heads baby bok choy, halved lengthwise
Optional: chili crisp on the table
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: Whisk sesame paste, soy, black vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil in a big bowl. Heat the neutral oil with sliced garlic and grated ginger over medium-low until the garlic is just pale gold, then pour the whole sizzling thing right into the sauce bowl and whisk until silky. Blanch the bok choy stems-down sixty seconds, flip, leaves twenty, shock cold and pat dry. Boil noodles, drain, toss in the sauce while still warm. For the dumplings, arrange them flat-side-down in a hot nonstick pan with two tablespoons oil and sear two minutes until deep gold, pour the cornstarch slurry in, clamp the lid on, steam seven minutes, then uncover and let the water evaporate until it sizzles silent. Pile noodles on the plate, bok choy around them, dumplings crust-up on the side, scallions and sesame seeds and cilantro on top. Ten minutes and it looks like it came out of a restaurant window.

variations.name: Cold Peanut Noodles with Cucumber

recipe_cards.name: Homemade Pizza Night
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
1 lb fresh mozzarella, hand-torn and patted dry
Toppings: rotisserie chicken, roasted red peppers, red onion, hot honey, ricotta, sautéed greens, Parmigiano
Baby arugula, lemon, olive oil, and flaky salt for side salad
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: Mix flour, water, salt, and that tiny pinch of yeast in a bowl until there are no dry bits, cover, and forget about it on the counter for an hour, then stretch and fold a couple times and put it in the fridge for at least a day, two is better. When you're ready, pull the dough out ninety minutes before you bake. Crank the oven to 550 with a baking steel on the lowest rack for a full forty-five minutes, no cheating. For sauce, blitz whole San Marzanos with olive oil, salt, a pinch of sugar, grated garlic, and a basil stem for five seconds only, you want it chunky. Stretch dough by hand on a semolina-dusted peel, top fast, launch fast, bake five to seven minutes until the cornicione is blistered and spotty. Finish each pie AFTER the oven with torn basil, good olive oil, hot honey, or lemon zest depending on which one it is. If you're using pre-shredded bag mozzarella for pizza night we are not related.

variations.name: Detroit-Style Pan Pizza
variations.description: Press the same cold-fermented dough into an oiled steel pan, layer brick cheese all the way to the edges for a lacy crust, and finish with red sauce striped on top.

variations.name: Grilled Pizza

variations.name: Focaccia Pizza (Pizza in Teglia)
variations.description: Use a higher-hydration focaccia dough pressed into a sheet pan, top with sauce and cheese, and bake for a thick, airy, almost-bread Roman-style pizza.

recipe_cards.name: Whole Roasted Branzino with Sautéed Kale and Creamy Polenta
ingredients: 2 whole branzino (about 1 to 1 1/4 lb each), scaled and gutted
1 lemon, thinly sliced, plus more for serving
3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
2 cups water or light chicken stock
1 large bunch lacinato (Tuscan) kale, stems removed, leaves torn
Salsa verde: 1 cup flat-leaf parsley, 2 tablespoons capers, 2 anchovy fillets, 1 small garlic clove, zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1/2 cup olive oil, red pepper flake
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: Score each fish three times per side on a 45-degree angle, deep enough to hit the flesh but not through it. Stuff the belly with lemon slices, thyme, smashed garlic, and a pinch of fennel seed, brush skin with olive oil, salt it generously inside and out. Roast on a preheated sheet pan at 450 for eighteen to twenty-two minutes until the skin is papery crisp and the flesh at the backbone flakes with a fork. Polenta wants time, so start it first in a heavy pot with milk and water, whisk the cornmeal in, and stir low and slow for thirty-five minutes before finishing with butter and Parmigiano off the heat. Hot pan, olive oil, smashed garlic, red pepper flake, toss the kale in for three minutes until the edges char, squeeze lemon. Whisk parsley, capers, anchovy, garlic, lemon, and olive oil for your salsa verde. Carve the fish at the table, spoon salsa verde over everything, and watch three people fight over the crispy skin. Good fish does not need a sauce from a jar.

variations.name: Salt-Crusted Whole Branzino
variations.description: Bury the fish in a mound of kosher salt mixed with egg white and roast. Crack open at the table for impossibly moist, perfectly seasoned fish.

variations.name: Acqua Pazza (Fish in Crazy Water)
variations.description: Poach branzino fillets in a light broth of tomatoes, white wine, garlic, and chili. Southern Italian fishermen style, lighter and brothier than the roast.

variations.name: Grilled Branzino with Herb Salad
variations.description: Grill the whole fish over hot coals for smoky char, then serve with a pile of fresh herb salad dressed in lemon and olive oil instead of salsa verde.

recipe_cards.name: Build-Your-Own Taco Night
ingredients: 1 1/4 lb ground beef (85/15) or ground turkey
1 15-oz can black beans, drained (crisped in olive oil with cumin and salt)
Small handful cilantro, plus more for serving
1/2 red onion, thinly sliced (for quick pickle)
4 Roma tomatoes, half a white onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 chipotle in adobo (for charred salsa)
1 cup crumbled queso fresco or cotija
1/4 cup toasted pepitas or crushed tortilla chips
Kid-friendly shredded cheddar on the side
recipe_cards.mamma_karen: Broil the tomatoes, half-onion, and garlic cloves on a sheet pan eight minutes until blistered black in spots, then blend with a chipotle and salt for a real charred salsa roja. Toss thin red onion slices with lime juice and salt, ten minutes and they go pink and gentle. Blitz avocado, sour cream, cilantro, and lime for the crema, done in thirty seconds. Brown the beef hard in a skillet with onion, garlic, and those warm spices, deglaze with a splash of water, simmer five minutes until glossy. Crisp the black beans in another pan with a little olive oil and cumin so they get a chewy edge. Toast the tortillas over the gas flame fifteen seconds a side until they puff and char, wrap in a towel to stay soft. Set the whole circus on the table, little bowls of everything, and let your girl build her own. That is half the fun and zero of the arguing.

variations.name: Tacos Al Pastor (Pork-Free Chicken Version)
variations.description: Marinate chicken thighs in guajillo, pineapple juice, and achiote for a weeknight spin on al pastor. Serve with charred pineapple and white onion.

variations.name: Fish Tacos with Cabbage Slaw
variations.description: Swap ground beef for flaky white fish seasoned with chili-lime and pan-fried. Top with crunchy cabbage slaw and chipotle crema for Baja beach-town vibes.

variations.name: Crispy Black Bean and Cheese Tacos
variations.description: Skip the meat entirely. Smash refried black beans and melty cheese into a folded tortilla and pan-fry until both sides are deeply crispy. Endlessly kid-approved.
